query: Whatever You're Having Whatever you order at the Gilded Newt, half the bar orders next, and the landlady has noticed. She leans over the counter. "Do me a favour, love. Order the elderflower fizz. I've forty bottles of it in the cellar and nobody's touched one since midsummer. There's a cut in it for you." The whole bar is waiting to see what you'll have. "One elderflower fizz, please." The fizz has been in the cellar since midsummer for a reason. Half the bar orders one after you, and half the bar spends the rest of the evening outside. The landlady gives you your cut anyway. By morning everyone knows whose idea it was. You raise a glass of fizz to the bar, and the bar raises forty back. It is far too sweet. For the rest of the term it's what people drink at the Newt, and every few weeks the landlady presses a small purse of coppers into your hand. Order what you always have You order your usual. So does half the bar. The landlady sighs, says "Traitor" quite fondly, and goes down to the cellar for more of it. The fizz stays where it is.
